I don't have any notes on Psalm 150 for you yet. My first attempt to fetch the commentary pages crashed because of a bug in my own code, and I then reached this turn's limit on web tool calls before I could try again. I didn't read a single source, and since every point has to come from a page I actually read and include its URL, I've left the notes out rather than write them from memory.

These are the pages I'll start with when you ask me to continue:

- **Verse-by-verse traditional readings:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-150/
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/150.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/150.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/150.htm
  - preceptaustin.org's Psalm 150 page
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** I'll look mainly at verses 3–5. The likely questions are whether instruments belong in worship (some Reformed writers argue for singing only the Psalms, without instruments), dancing (verse 4), and Pentecostal and charismatic expressive worship. I'll look for what each tradition's own teachers say on ligonier.org, gty.org, spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org, seedbed.com, ag.org, samstorms.org, lcms.org and 1517.org.
- **Other views:** netbible.org's translation notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship, plus newadvent.org (the Church Fathers on Psalm 150) and catholic.com or oca.org for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'll only mention a popular modern teaching if these sites actually discuss it.

If you reply "continue," I'll read the sources and write the notes verse by verse, with the URL after each point.
